description: Machine-readable conventions that hold for EVERY project, whatever its stack. One file, one section per topic; a topic moves here from prose when a tool can read it. Profile-dependent values do not belong here: they live in the stack profiles (shared/profiles/*.json, and .shipwright/profiles/ for a project's own), which refine these conventions, never contradict them. Sections today: skill_authoring (the machine-readable half of docs/building-skills-plugins-agents.md) and constitution (how each rule of shared/constitution.md is enforced; an inventory of Shipwright's own enforcement kept here so the rules and their register sit beside each other). The architecture rules stay stack-profile keys for now: only one profile carries them.

skill_authoring.description: The numeric limits and the alignment with Anthropic's 'Skill authoring best practices' (platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices, read 2026-11-15). The four rules themselves are prose and live only in docs/building-skills-plugins-agents.md, which explains and links and repeats no number here. Read by shared/scripts/tools/check_skill_authoring.py. On any conflict the Shipwright rule wins.

every reference file is linked from SKILL.md; a reference that links on to another reference file makes Claude preview it with head and read it incompletely

constitution.description: How each rule of shared/constitution.md is enforced. One entry per rule unit, matched by a hash of the rule text; shared/scripts/lib/constitution_register.py checks it, shared/tests/test_constitution_register.py fails on drift. Enforcement vocabulary is closed: hook, validator, test, prompt-only (mechanisable), prompt-only (judgement), unimplemented. Judgement rules are never turned into gates and no coverage number is computed.
